messages:
pagerduty-bot: URGENT: PAGER -> SRE oncall. Smart routing policy mismatch detected. Rule: customer.residency == EU should route -> eu-west-1. Observed: ~2% of requests with residency=EU routed to us-east-1 for ~18m. Risk: data residency policy violated for affected requests. Incident created: INC-180212.
maya: acked. I'm on call and stepping in. Paging history shows automatic fallback triggered at 2026-03-15T09:02:43Z. @jonas can you pull the routing policy diff? :eyes:
jonas: pulling it now. small note: the canary fallback config was recently changed by infra runbook to allow cross-region fallback for latency-sensitive customers. I'm checking git. Give me 2m.
ops-bot: deploy-log: rollout smart-routing-v3 -> canary at 2026-03-15T08:59:12Z by infra-automation. Config id: cfg_9b7a.
jonas: found it. cfg_9b7a introduced fallback_priority: [region, model_variant] and a fallback_allow_cross_region: true flag for low-latency profiles. The residency policy code path is supposed to blacklist cross-region for residency=EU but the condition was inverted (e.g., if (!residency) => allow). Reproducing locally.
azra: oncall SRE (secondary) here. If it's routing to us-east, we need to disable cross-region fallback immediately and re-route impacted requests back to eu-west. Maya, do you want me to flip the flag in the control plane or block the new canary? I can also push a temporary rule to drop cross-region fallbacks.
maya: flip the flag in the control plane first then roll back canary if needed. Priority: stop further violations, then audit affected customers. @ellie please standby for CS impact notes.
jonas: executing control-plane toggle now. Command:
```
redwoodctl config set cfg_9b7a fallback_allow_cross_region false --reason "emergency - residency violation"
```
jonas: command returned 200. Control plane acknowledged. Applying change to canary and global.
ops-bot: config-update: cfg_9b7a.fallback_allow_cross_region=false applied at 2026-03-15T09:06:12Z to canary group, propagation to global starting.
maya: good. I'm seeing a drop in cross-region routes in the routing metrics. Query:
```
select count(*) from routing_logs where residency='EU' and region!='eu-west-1' and ts > now() - interval '30 minutes';
```
maya: result: 0 after 2026-03-15T09:07:10Z. The misrouted window appears to be 08:49:12Z -> 09:06:12Z (17m). We need to capture request ids for replay/audit.
jonas: pulling logs and will export request ids (masked) for compliance. Command:
```
redwoodctl logs export --filter "residency:EU AND region:us-east-1 AND ts:2026-03-15T08:49..2026-03-15T09:06" --anonymize --format jsonl --out /tmp/eu-misroute.jsonl
```
jonas: export complete. ~34k requests, ~2.1% of EU traffic in that window. Saving a secure copy to ops vault.
azra: running quick customer impact scan against tenant metadata. Early results: 7 enterprise tenants with residency enforcement enabled saw >0 incidents; none are flagged as regulated-high (banking/health) in metadata but some are EU-fintechs. @ellie can you draft an initial CS message template? We should prepare to reach out proactively.
ellie: drafting. Proposed: short apology, summary of actions taken, mitigation, what we're doing to ensure this doesn't recur, offer timeline for forensics. Will share in a minute.
maya: also, we need to check whether the model variant selection logic contributed. There's a secondary issue: during fallback the routing selects a compatible model_variant (quantized-cpu) in us-east which may have different privacy annotations in our metadata - confirm that model variant doesn't leak any additional telemetry. @jonas can you verify model variant metadata? 
jonas: checking model catalog. The canary also introduced a model-variant mapping change: for small seq lengths, prefer variant q4_0_cpu in fallback. q4_0_cpu has 'hosted_in' attribute set to host_region (us-east-1). No extra telemetry. But visibility is limited — I'll record the mapping mismap: model_map_v12 contains a default host_region: us-east for fallback variants.
maya: ok. Primary compliance violation is region, not model telemetry. Still record both in the post-incident notes.
ops-bot: pagerduty-bot: automatic escalation to SEV-1 at 2026-03-15T09:10:05Z due to policy breach > 15m.
jonas: I will start a limited replay test to verify no further cross-region routing. Running in staging with the updated flag.

jonas: replay script:
```
python -m tests.replay --input /tmp/eu-misroute.jsonl --target-region eu-west-1 --dry-run
```
jonas: dry-run shows 100% routing to eu-west-1.
azra: good. Next, we need to coordinate customer notifications and legal/compliance review. @maya can you call out any tenants that require immediate notification? Ellie will handle comms. I will prepare artifacts for legal.
maya: immediate-notify list: tenant_42 (EU-fintech), tenant_77 (SaaS-eu), tenant_140 (analytics-eu). CS to send initial notice within 2 hours. Legal loop-in required if any PII suspected — assign to legal on call.
ellie: initial message drafted:
"Hi <tenant>,
We detected a configuration issue where some requests with EU data residency were briefly routed outside the EU (us-east-1) between 08:49 and 09:06 UTC on 2026-03-15. We have disabled the fallback causing this, reverted the config, and are performing a full audit. No evidence of data exfiltration; we are preserving logs and will share a detailed report within 48 hours. Apologies for the disruption. - Redwood Inference"

maya: looks good. Add a note we will offer a call if they want to review logs.
ellie: added. Sending now to the three tenants and CS will post to account dashboards.

pagerduty-bot: note: initial on-call handoff scheduled in 2h. Current oncall: maya -> handoff to azra at 11:00 UTC.
azra: I'll take the 11:00 handoff and hold the incident lead if it isn't fully mitigated. Also preparing postmortem template: include root cause, diff snippet, timeline, blast radius, remediation (code + process), and verification steps.
maya: writing quick root cause: accidental inversion of residency check in new canary config (cfg_9b7a) allowed cross-region fallbacks for some residency-tagged requests. Secondary: model variant mapping defaulted host_region to us-east for fallback variants.
maya: immediate remediation completed: cfg toggle + rollback scheduled for canary. Preventative items:
- add unit test for residency check condition
- add end-to-end synthetic tests for residency enforcement
- disallow fallback_allow_cross_region for any config with residency policies unless explicitly whitelisted
- require a security sign-off for changes to routing fallbacks

jonas: I'll open 2 PRs: one for unit test, one for canary gating change. ETA EOD.
azra: I'll start collecting artifacts for postmortem and compliance package. Also schedule a brief sync with Legal and CS in 30m.

maya: marking incident as Mitigated -> cross-region toggled and propagation verified. Still open for post-incident review and customer comms. Severity: S1 -> compliance breach, but contained. Will attach logs and timeline to INC-180212.
ellie: CS messages sent to tenants; 2 tenants requested calls, booked for today.

pagerduty-bot: INC-180212 status changed: Mitigated at 2026-03-15T09:18:45Z. Postmortem_assignee: azra.

maya: thanks team. Azra, take lead on postmortem. Jonas, follow-up PRs. Ellie, compile comms artifacts and CS notes. Will schedule a 40m post-incident review at 15:00 UTC.
azra: acknowledged. I will include the control-plane diff and the exact inverted condition snippet in the postmortem. Closing slack thread after postmortem is published.

ops-bot: reminder: add incident tag "residency-policy-violation" to INC-180212 in the tracker.

maya: closing notes: no customer data confirmed exfiltrated; retained all logs; legal looped in. Thanks everyone :heart:
